title: I married the 'life of the party' and ended up miserable. His traits I found intoxicating at 26 repulsed me in my forties. This is my warning before saying 'I do'…
text:
“I don’t know how you’re going to endure for the next 50 years,” the waitress joked on our first wedding anniversary.
In front of me, my husband Jack* continued with a drink in the hand, life and soul of the party.
While I knew he was quite noisy and perhaps a bit annoying, he didn’t mean any damage.
In fact, I found its excitable nature when we met a few years before, in the mid -twenties.
Jack was fun, lovely and a great beser. He spoke to a million miles per hour and could never concentrate on one thing for a long time, but that was part of what made him so fun and spontaneous.
He also had a big heart. Sweet, kind, close to his parents … The list of great qualities continued and continued.
So I smiled at the waitress, I put my eyes on simulated irritation and enjoyed the rest of the night celebrating my first anniversary with my fool and entertaining husband.
Twenty -four years and two children later, the waitress’s comment had begun to sound painfully true.
Now in my 50s and single, I would like to choose the ‘boring guy’ instead of the ‘life of the party’ (stock image raised by the models)
Jack’s inability to concentrate on anything for a long time meant that he had spent two decades jumping from one job to another, never holding one, never forging a real career.
Meanwhile, I worked on three jobs, with up to 100 hours a week, to keep a roof on our heads and dinner on the table.
Speaking of dinner, my ‘husband of the house’ part -time could not handle that.
I would give him a shopping list and ask him to do the groceries while I was at work. But he would call me repeatedly from the supermarket, wanting to hold his hand throughout the task, unable to follow basic instructions.
Even when I managed to buy the ingredients for dinner, they were sitting without touching at the bank when I entered the door exhausted.
‘Couldn’t you have started at dinner?’ I would sigh.
“I didn’t know the recipe,” he shrugged.
The only two recipes I knew were Spaghetti Bolognese and Pizza, and always praised each time he made the same dish.
I found myself in my fifty years, dealing with a chronic health condition that could limit my sexual life, with zero support from my husband (stock image raised by models)
Nor did I know how to order or wash clothes, as is the case. I would always find wet clothes in the washing machine or at the basket hoping to be put in the line.
For years I felt that I had a third child to feed, clean and care for.
As my real children matured until adulthood, leaving Jack in his path, they began to notice it too.
‘Mom, communicates as a teenager. He will growl or send a text message with the answers of a word: ‘My daughter, now 21 years old, complained to me.
Make my daughter tell me that about her own father was deeply shameful.
Jack absolutely adored children and was a good father, but as a husband was a complete and absolute disappointment; The definition of a ‘son-son’.
Needless to say, feeling that her husband is her son, not her equal, not long for libido. Our sex life dried when I stopped finding his funny funny jokes.
I tried to talk to him, explaining how I felt, but it is useless. ‘I didn’t!’ In general, they were the first words outside Jack’s mouth when I tried to address something serious. As a mischievous child who has been accused of stealing a kitchen cookie.

In 2020, our marriage reached the point of no return.
I was working ridiculous hours, doing all domestic tasks, taking care of children (including Jack), the responsibility of absolutely everything fell on my shoulders and stress began to affect my health.
My skin got painfully itching and did not sleep well at night. At first, I blamed menopause, but when irritating lesions began to spread more about my body, I went to see the doctor.
I was surprised that a rare skin disease called lincoln sclerosis.
The painful eruptions with itching were the main symptom, but it was even more horrified when the doctor told me that the patches could spread to my genitals, making sex painful or even impossible.
While there were treatments such as topical steroids, the condition would probably affect me for the rest of my life.
The cause of the condition was largely unknown, but it was known that stress exacerbated it.
It was the call of attention I needed.
Now I was in my fifty years, dealing with a chronic health condition that could limit my sexual life, with zero my husband’s support.
Not only that, but it was the main cause of stress that my already painful condition would get worse.
I knew this was not what I wanted, or needed, for the rest of my life.
“I can’t do this anymore,” I told Jack a few months later. Shortly after, I requested divorce.
Leaving a marriage without sex and finding me single in my fifty years, with a condition that could affect my ability to have sex in the future, I felt miserable.
I had lost so many years with Jack and now my years of intimacy could be behind me. It was so unfair.
That said, I felt too vulnerable to immerse a foot in the foot pool. Then I did not socialize much, and the applications terrified me, as well as the idea of ​​explaining the nature of my skin condition to a new couple.
“You could always think about hiring an escort,” my friend suggested one night after a couple of wine drinks.
At first I laughed at his suggestion, but as time passed, curiosity surpassed me.
I started Google Escort agencies and found His confidant who was directed by a passionate woman for making an escort an enriching experience.
I picked up the courage to reserve and appointment, and it didn’t disappoint me!
In the hours I spent with my escort, they gave me more attention, care and consideration than throughout my marriage.
My warning to other women is this: marrying the life of the party may seem like a good idea in their veins. But when the party ends, you could regret it.
*The name has been changed
